messages.subject: RIFF info in wav files
parts:
I have a bunch of wav files in which the date and time
of the recording are included at the begining of the file.

If I do (in linux):
$ head -c 1024 STE-077.wav
I get a mixture of ascii and binary within which I can see the date:
RIFF�e WAVEbextZ ZOOM Handy Recorder H4n2013-08-1509:38:52���A=PCM,F=96000,W=24,M=stereo,T=ZOOM Handy Recorder H4nfmt

Unfortunately, I cannot find the way to get rid of the binary parts.
Tried saving the output of head to a text file i.e.
$ head -c 1024 STE-077.wav > a.txt

My ultimate goal is to rename the file to, ie
STE-077_2013-08-15-09:38:52.wav

Once I could get the text part of a.txt in R it would be very simple,
but I've tried read.table(), scan(), readBin() etc with a.txt with no success.

Could I read this information with seewave from the wav file?
I've tried with readWave(), but the RIFF part seems ignored.

Thanks

Agus

maintainer of tuneR if necessary.

appropriate regular expression to specify that you want the text
between 'H4n' and '???' (sorry I cannot help with regular
expressions). Then you can use file.rename() to rename your file with
the date.

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] RIFF info in wav files
parts:
Hi!

Just got an idea from a colleague that is going to solve the problem:

Hi,

I think you are almost there. The problem is that the recorder is adding some metadata that is not based on the standard, so this has to be customized.

Just add a substring extraction if the position stays the same. The first number is where it starts and the second number is how many letters to use:

======
$ filehead=$(head -c 1024 STE-077.wav)
$ echo ${filehead:40:10}

2013-08-15

$ echo ${filehead:50:8}

09:38:52
======

You should be able to run this from R using the function system().
